clue.text: Zeal shown by a monarch of sullen nature

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for rex or regina, a king or queen
a dour person is gloomy and sullen by temperament

explanation.surface: Someone notes the fervour displayed by a grumpy king.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardour is passionate enthusiasm, the same eager fervour as zeal.

clue.text: A mariner returned holding oriental noose

indicators.note: holding means the reversed letters wrap round the next piece
returned means the pair of words a and mariner, as letters, are read backwards

parts.note: a tar is an old slang word for a sailor
E stands for east, so oriental gives E

explanation.surface: A sailor comes home carrying a rope loop picked up in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns A + TAR into RATA, and 'holding' puts E inside it after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: A reata is a lariat, a rope with a running loop used to catch livestock.

clue.text: Moan in public after careless blunder

indicators.note: in means the word for a moan is placed inside the word for public

parts.note: overt means done openly, in public
a sigh is a low moan of sorrow or weariness

explanation.surface: Someone groans openly after making a slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is only a link joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An oversight is a mistake made through failing to notice something.

clue.text: Serviceman placed in correct order of rank

indicators.note: placed in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A soldier is slotted into the proper place in the ranking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serviceman' suggests a soldier, but here it is a cleric who takes church services; the letters run across 'corRECT ORder'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rector is a parish priest who leads church services.

clue.text: Printed material isn't easy to duplicate

parts.note: something that is not easy is hard
to duplicate something is to copy it

explanation.surface: A complaint that printed documents are difficult to reproduce.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard copy is a paper printout as opposed to an electronic version.

clue.text: Admonish male for producing insoluble problem

indicators.note: producing suggests these letters are worked up into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Telling off a man creates a situation with no good way out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'producing' rearranges the letters of ADMONISH MALE FOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the horns of a dilemma means facing two equally bad choices, a problem with no good solution.

clue.text: Kept back to be dished up again

explanation.surface: Food set aside so that it can be served a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the word as RE-SERVED, served once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held in reserve is kept back; split as re-served it means served at table a second time.

clue.text: Man in headgear of poor quality

indicators.note: in means the word for man goes inside the word for headgear

parts.note: a cap is a simple piece of headgear
he is the pronoun for a male, so man gives he

explanation.surface: A fellow wearing a shoddy hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap goods are inexpensive and often shoddy or inferior.

clue.text: Reverie for flautist? Vain hope!

explanation.surface: A musician's daydream dismissed as a fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is playful: a flautist plays a pipe, so their daydream is a dream of the pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe dream is an unrealistic fantasy, originally from opium-pipe visions; a flute is a kind of pipe.

clue.text: Redcaps involved with OTC, for example?

definitions.text: Redcaps involved with OTC, for example?

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters are entangled and mixed up together

explanation.surface: Military police are mixed up with a university officer training unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges REDCAPS plus OTC. Redcaps are British military police; the OTC, the Officers' Training Corps for students, is itself an example of what the whole clue defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The Officers' Training Corps is a body giving young people military training, the kind of unit called a cadet corps.

clue.text: Detect cars from el Salvador and Paraguay?

parts.note: ES is the international vehicle registration code shown on cars from El Salvador
PY is Paraguay's international vehicle registration code

explanation.surface: Spotting vehicles that come from two Latin American countries.
explanation.walkthrough: International car codes are the stickers on cars driven abroad: ES for El Salvador, PY for Paraguay.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of or spot something.

clue.text: Instruments shortly to be housed by singer

indicators.note: to be housed by means the word for shortly sits inside the word for singer

parts.note: a bass is a singer with the lowest male voice
soon means shortly, before long

explanation.surface: Wind instruments are soon to be stored at a vocalist's home.
explanation.definitionFit: Bassoons are deep-toned woodwind instruments.

clue.text: They may be shot by coppers during swoops

indicators.note: during means the coins go inside the word for swoops, in the midst of them

parts.note: police swoops are raids
P stands for pence, the copper coins

explanation.surface: Police officers taking fire while carrying out sudden raids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' wants to be police, chiming with 'swoops', but it means copper coins, pennies.
explanation.definitionFit: Canoeists shoot the rapids, riding fast through turbulent stretches of river.

clue.text: Hit by a bullet

explanation.surface: Someone struck by gunfire.
explanation.definitionFit: To slug is to punch hard; a slug is also slang for a bullet.

clue.text: Made thugs toil to deliver last post

indicators.note: made means these letters are put together into a new form

explanation.surface: Ruffians were forced to labour so they could carry the final delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made' rearranges THUGS TOIL. The Last Post is the military bugle call at day's end, here as a call meaning bedtime, not mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Lights out is the bugle call or signal at night telling troops to sleep, like the final call of the day.

clue.text: Students revive around the end of term

indicators.note: around means the word for revive surrounds the next piece

parts.note: to freshen is to revive or refresh

indicators.note: the end of picks out the final letter of the word term

explanation.surface: Undergraduates perk up as the term closes.
explanation.definitionFit: Freshmen are first-year students at a college or university.

clue.text: Sheltered bower he would go around

indicators.note: go around means the contraction for he would is placed round the word for bower

parts.note: he would contracts to he'd
an arbour is a leafy shaded bower in a garden

explanation.surface: A man would walk round a garden retreat that gave him shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bower' suggests a lady's private chamber or a leafy nook; the setter wants its garden-shelter sense, and 'he would' must be contracted.
explanation.definitionFit: To harbour someone is to give them refuge, so harboured means gave shelter.

clue.text: No-one returned to stable it

parts.note: a stall is a compartment for a horse in a stable

indicators.note: returned means the letters of no-one, read as no plus one, run backwards

parts.note: split as no plus one, with one as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Nobody came back to put the horse away.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'No-one' as two words, the second being the Roman numeral for one; the whole clue doubles as a hint to the horse you would put in a stable.
explanation.definitionFit: A stallion is an uncastrated male horse, an animal that is kept in a stable.

clue.text: Shaken up when dolt dined and died

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Shaken up when dolt dined and died', gives only GIT + ATE + D: the A of AGITATED is missing (presumably 'a dolt'), and 'when' cannot supply it; no source found.
annotationWithheld.clue: Shaken up when dolt dined and died

clue.text: Scam involving soft butter initially

indicators.note: initially says the butting animal comes first, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: a ram butts with its head, so it is a butter
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

explanation.surface: A fraud involving the first of some soft butter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' reads as the dairy spread, but it is one who butts, a ram. RAMP is British slang for a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramp in British slang is a swindle, especially one that inflates prices.

clue.text: Nervous of falling over the precipice

explanation.surface: Anxious about toppling off the cliff.
explanation.definitionFit: On edge means tense or jumpy; literally it also describes being at the brink, close to a drop.

clue.text: A fabric produced as one wishes

parts.note: twill is a cloth woven with diagonal ridges

explanation.surface: A cloth made to whatever pattern the customer likes.
explanation.definitionFit: At will means whenever or however one chooses.

clue.text: Trader's self-description is perfect

explanation.surface: A merchant says his own description is flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits as I DEAL, what a trader would say about themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal means perfect or best possible; split as two words it is a dealer's statement of what they do.

clue.text: Solitary fellow embraces fellow capitalist

indicators.note: embraces means the word for a solitary fellow wraps round the next piece

parts.note: a loner is someone who prefers to be alone
a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: A recluse hugs a fellow who is a financier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capitalist' looks like a financier but means someone from the capital, London.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lives in Britain's capital city is a resident of London.

clue.text: Consumed some great English dishes

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is taken, letters lying inside them

explanation.surface: Someone has gobbled up a few fine British dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has been eaten has been consumed.

clue.text: Drill needed when tidal wave occurs

explanation.surface: Advice on boring equipment during a surge of sea water.
explanation.definitionFit: To bore is to drill a hole; a bore is also a surge wave travelling up a river on the tide.

clue.text: Excessive organising made me riot

indicators.note: organising suggests the letters are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone protests that overzealous planning drove them to rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: Immoderate means going beyond reasonable limits, so excessive.

clue.text: Fabulous runner gains top award in Georgian capital

indicators.note: in means the award letter is placed inside the name of the city

parts.note: Atlanta is the capital of the US state of Georgia
A is the top grade, the highest mark awarded

explanation.surface: An athlete wins first prize in a southern US city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Georgian' suggests the country in the Caucasus, but it is the US state. 'Fabulous' means from myth: Atalanta was the swift huntress of Greek legend.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Atalanta was a famously swift huntress who raced her suitors.

clue.text: Finishing up as a big noise in England

indicators.note: in means the word for big noise goes inside the abbreviation for England

parts.note: a din is a loud racket

explanation.surface: Someone ends up as a celebrity back in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big noise' suggests a VIP but means a loud din.
explanation.definitionFit: An ending is the finish or conclusion of something.
